The main issues for macOS are:

1. **Backslash path separators** - Mac uses forward slashes `/`
2. **`Dir$()` wildcard** - works, but path handling differs
3. **`FileDialog`** - different constants on Mac

Here's a corrected version:

```vba
Sub SaveAllAsPDF()
    Dim strPath As String
    Dim oDoc As Document
    Dim fDialog As FileDialog
    Dim strFilename As String
    Dim strDocName As String

    ' Use FileDialog for folder selection
    Set fDialog = Application.FileDialog(msoFileDialogFolderPicker)
    With fDialog
        .Title = "Select folder to save PDF files"
        .AllowMultiSelect = False
        If .Show <> -1 Then Exit Sub
    End With

    strPath = fDialog.SelectedItems.Item(1)
    ' Convert Mac path format (ensure trailing colon for folder)
    If Right(strPath, 1) <> ":" Then strPath = strPath & ":"

    ' Close all documents prompting to save changes
    On Error Resume Next
    Documents.Close SaveChanges:=wdPromptToSaveChanges
    On Error GoTo 0

    ' Get first DOC file
    strFilename = Dir$(strPath & "*.doc")
    
    While Len(strFilename) <> 0
        Set oDoc = Documents.Open(strPath & strFilename)
        
        ' Extract filename without extension
        strDocName = Left(oDoc.Name, InStrRev(oDoc.Name, ".") - 1)
        
        ' Save as PDF
        oDoc.ExportAsFixedFormat OutputFileName:=strPath & strDocName & ".pdf", _
                                 ExportFormat:=wdExportFormatPDF, _
                                 OpenAfterExport:=False
        
        ' Close without saving
        oDoc.Close SaveChanges:=wdDoNotSaveChanges
        
        strFilename = Dir$()
    Wend
    
    MsgBox "PDF export complete!", vbInformation
End Sub
```

**Key changes for Mac:**

| Issue | Windows | Mac |
|-------|---------|-----|
| Path separator | `\` | `:` (in VBA) |
| Path ending | `\` | `:` |
| `Dir$()` | `\*.*` | `*.doc` (works same) |

If you want a truly universal version that detects the platform automatically:

```vba
Sub SaveAllAsPDF()
    Dim strPath As String, oDoc As Document
    Dim fDialog As FileDialog, strFilename As String, strDocName As String
    Dim isMac As Boolean
    
    ' Detect platform
    #If Mac Then
        isMac = True
    #Else
        isMac = False
    #End If

    Set fDialog = Application.FileDialog(msoFileDialogFolderPicker)
    With fDialog
        .Title = "Select folder to save PDF files"
        .AllowMultiSelect = False
        If .Show <> -1 Then Exit Sub
    End With

    strPath = fDialog.SelectedItems.Item(1)
    If isMac Then
        If Right(strPath, 1) <> ":" Then strPath = strPath & ":"
    Else
        If Right(strPath, 1) <> "\" Then strPath = strPath & "\"
    End If

    On Error Resume Next
    Documents.Close SaveChanges:=wdPromptToSaveChanges
    On Error GoTo 0

    strFilename = Dir$(strPath & "*.doc")
    
    While Len(strFilename) <> 0
        Set oDoc = Documents.Open(strPath & strFilename)
        strDocName = Left(oDoc.Name, InStrRev(oDoc.Name, ".") - 1)
        
        oDoc.ExportAsFixedFormat OutputFileName:=strPath & strDocName & ".pdf", _
                                 ExportFormat:=wdExportFormatPDF, _
                                 OpenAfterExport:=False
        
        oDoc.Close SaveChanges:=wdDoNotSaveChanges
        strFilename = Dir$()
    Wend
    
    MsgBox "PDF export complete!", vbInformation
End Sub
```

**Note:** Word VBA on Mac can be finicky. Make sure:
- Word has permission to access files in System Preferences > Security & Privacy > Privacy > Files and Folders
- The `.doc` files are not corrupted

Correct — `msoFileDialogFolderPicker` can be unreliable or behave differently on Word for Mac. Here's a workaround using `MacScript` to call the native macOS file picker:

```vba
Function SelectFolderMac() As String
    Dim script As String
    script = "POSIX path of (choose folder with prompt ""Select folder to save PDF files"")"
    On Error Resume Next
    SelectFolderMac = MacScript(script)
    On Error GoTo 0
End Function

Sub SaveAllAsPDF()
    Dim strPath As String, oDoc As Document
    Dim strFilename As String, strDocName As String

    ' Get folder using native Mac dialog
    strPath = SelectFolderMac()
    If strPath = "" Then
        MsgBox "No folder selected. Exiting.", vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Ensure trailing slash
    If Right(strPath, 1) <> "/" Then strPath = strPath & "/"

    ' Close all documents
    On Error Resume Next
    Documents.Close SaveChanges:=wdPromptToSaveChanges
    On Error GoTo 0

    ' Process DOC files
    strFilename = Dir$(strPath & "*.doc")
    
    While Len(strFilename) <> 0
        Set oDoc = Documents.Open(strPath & strFilename)
        strDocName = Left(oDoc.Name, InStrRev(oDoc.Name, ".") - 1)
        
        oDoc.ExportAsFixedFormat OutputFileName:=strPath & strDocName & ".pdf", _
                                 ExportFormat:=wdExportFormatPDF, _
                                 OpenAfterExport:=False
        
        oDoc.Close SaveChanges:=wdDoNotSaveChanges
        strFilename = Dir$()
    Wend
    
    MsgBox "PDF export complete!", vbInformation
End Sub
```

**Key changes:**
| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| `FileDialog` unreliable on Mac | Use `MacScript` with `choose folder` |
| Backslash paths | Use forward slash `/` on Mac |
| Missing `strDocName` declaration | Added `Dim strDocName As String` |

This should work on both platforms now — the `choose folder` AppleScript command is the standard way to select folders in macOS Office applications.

There are a few common issues with `ExportAsFixedFormat` on Mac. Let me add debugging and try an alternative method:

```vba
Function SelectFolderMac() As String
    Dim script As String
    script = "POSIX path of (choose folder with prompt ""Select folder to save PDF files"")"
    On Error Resume Next
    SelectFolderMac = MacScript(script)
    On Error GoTo 0
End Function

Sub SaveAllAsPDF()
    Dim strPath As String, oDoc As Document
    Dim strFilename As String, strDocName As String
    Dim pdfPath As String
    Dim errCount As Integer
    
    errCount = 0
    
    ' Get folder using native Mac dialog
    strPath = SelectFolderMac()
    If strPath = "" Then
        MsgBox "No folder selected. Exiting.", vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    ' Ensure trailing slash (Mac POSIX paths use /)
    If Right(strPath, 1) <> "/" Then strPath = strPath & "/"

    ' Close all documents
    On Error Resume Next
    Documents.Close SaveChanges:=wdPromptToSaveChanges
    On Error GoTo 0

    ' Process DOC files
    strFilename = Dir$(strPath & "*.doc")
    
    If Len(strFilename) = 0 Then
        MsgBox "No .doc files found in:" & vbCrLf & strPath, vbExclamation
        Exit Sub
    End If
    
    While Len(strFilename) <> 0
        Set oDoc = Documents.Open(strPath & strFilename)
        strDocName = Left(oDoc.Name, InStrRev(oDoc.Name, ".") - 1)
        pdfPath = strPath & strDocName & ".pdf"
        
        ' Debug: show what's happening
        Debug.Print "Processing: " & strFilename
        Debug.Print "Output path: " & pdfPath
        
        ' Try ExportAsFixedFormat with error handling
        On Error Resume Next
        oDoc.ExportAsFixedFormat OutputFileName:=pdfPath, _
                                 ExportFormat:=wdExportFormatPDF, _
                                 OpenAfterExport:=False, _
                                 IncludeDocumentProperties:=True, _
                                 OptimizeFor:=wdExportOptimizeForPrint
                                 
        If Err.Number <> 0 Then
            errCount = errCount + 1
            MsgBox "Error exporting " & strDocName & ":" & vbCrLf & Err.Description, vbCritical
            Err.Clear
        End If
        On Error GoTo 0
        
        oDoc.Close SaveChanges:=wdDoNotSaveChanges
        strFilename = Dir$()
    Wend
    
    If errCount = 0 Then
        MsgBox "PDF export complete!", vbInformation
    Else
        MsgBox "Export complete with " & errCount & " error(s).", vbExclamation
    End If
End Sub
```

**What to check:**

1. **Run the macro and watch the Output window** (View → Immediate Window) — it will print each file being processed

2. **Common Mac issues:**
   - Word needs "Full Disk Access" in System Preferences → Security & Privacy → Privacy
   - The folder might be iCloud Drive which has sync issues
   - Try a local folder like Desktop first

3. **Alternative: Use `PrintOut` method** if `ExportAsFixedFormat` still fails:

```vba
' Replace the ExportAsFixedFormat call with this:
oDoc.PrintOut OutputFileName:=pdfPath, _
              PrintToFile:=True, _
              OutputFileName:=pdfPath, _
              PrintZoom:=100
```

Does the debug output show any files being processed, or do you get errors?

That's a very long path with Chinese characters (括号 = parentheses, 学校 = school, etc.) — this could be causing encoding issues.

**Try this first:** Test with a simple path like `/Users/sinchunyeung/Desktop/` to confirm the macro works at all.

If it works there, the issue is likely the special characters in the path. Here's a more robust version that handles Unicode:

```vba
Function SelectFolderMac() As String
    Dim script As String
    script = "POSIX path of (choose folder with prompt ""Select folder"")"
    On Error Resume Next
    SelectFolderMac = MacScript(script)
    On Error GoTo 0
End Function

Sub SaveAllAsPDF()
    Dim oDoc As Document
    Dim strFilename As String, strDocName As String
    Dim strPath As String, pdfPath As String
    Dim errCount As Integer, fileCount As Integer
    Dim fs As Object
    
    errCount = 0
    fileCount = 0
    
    ' Use native folder picker
    strPath = SelectFolderMac()
    If strPath = "" Then Exit Sub
    
    ' Convert HFS path to POSIX if needed (macOS sometimes returns : instead of /)
    If InStr(strPath, ":") > 0 Then
        strPath = Replace(strPath, ":", "/")
    End If
    
    ' Ensure trailing slash
    If Right(strPath, 1) <> "/" Then strPath = strPath & "/"
    
    MsgBox "Using folder:" & vbCrLf & strPath, vbInformation
    
    ' Use FileSystemObject for better Mac compatibility
    Set fs = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")
    
    ' Find first .doc file
    strFilename = Dir$(strPath & "*.doc")
    
    If Len(strFilename) = 0 Then
        strFilename = Dir$(strPath & "*.docx")
        If Len(strFilename) = 0 Then
            MsgBox "No .doc or .docx files found in:" & vbCrLf & strPath, vbExclamation
            Exit Sub
        End If
    End If
    
    While Len(strFilename) <> 0
        fileCount = fileCount + 1
        
        ' Full path for opening
        Dim fullPath As String
        fullPath = strPath & strFilename
        
        Set oDoc = Documents.Open(fullPath)
        strDocName = Left(oDoc.Name, InStrRev(oDoc.Name, ".") - 1)
        pdfPath = strPath & strDocName & ".pdf"
        
        Debug.Print "File " & fileCount & ": " & strFilename
        
        ' Export with explicit settings
        oDoc.ExportAsFixedFormat _
            OutputFileName:=pdfPath, _
            ExportFormat:=wdExportFormatPDF, _
            OpenAfterExport:=False
        
        oDoc.Close SaveChanges:=wdDoNotSaveChanges
        
        strFilename = Dir$()
    Wend
    
    MsgBox "Done! Processed " & fileCount & " file(s)." & vbCrLf & _
           "Errors: " & errCount, vbInformation
End Sub
```
